title: Lotte Biologics secures first manufacturing deal for US$3.3B Songdo Campus | HealthCare Middle East & Africa - No.1 Health & Pharma Manufacturing Industry Publication
summary: The Songdo Bio Campus will complement Lotte Biologics' existing manufacturing facility in Syracuse, New York.
thbAction: Use the article as an entry point to pitch THB's commercial visibility layer for territory planning, account prioritization, and next-best-action for pharma leadership teams.
contentHtml:
SOUTH KOREA—Lotte Biologics has secured its first manufacturing contract for its US$3.3 billion Songdo Bio Campus near Seoul, ahead of the facility’s planned commercial production launch in 2027.

The contract, announced on November 17, covers the manufacturing of both drug substances and finished pharmaceutical products for an undisclosed pharmaceutical company.

However, Lotte did not reveal the client’s identity or the financial terms of the agreement.

Local publication Chosun Biz reported that South Korean pharmaceutical manufacturer Celltrion could be the customer, although neither company has confirmed the speculation.

The agreement marks an important step in Lotte Biologics’ expansion into large-scale contract development and manufacturing organisation (CDMO) services.

The company expects its Songdo operations to generate at least KRW 1 trillion (US$753 million) in annual revenue by 2030.

James Park, co-CEO of Lotte Biologics, described the agreement as an endorsement of the company’s manufacturing strategy and its ability to meet customer requirements.

He said the company was developing an integrated manufacturing platform focused on quality, reliability and production speed.

Songdo campus expands manufacturing capacity

The Songdo Bio Campus will complement Lotte Biologics’ existing manufacturing facility in Syracuse, New York.

The US plant recently completed a US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) inspection without receiving any observations, according to the company.

Lotte acquired the Syracuse facility from Bristol Myers Squibb for US$160 million in 2023 as part of its entry into the CDMO market.

The Songdo campus will cover approximately 2.2 million square feet and comprise three manufacturing plants with a combined bioreactor capacity of 360,000 litres, alongside supporting infrastructure.

Plant 1, which has a capacity of 120,000 litres across eight 15,000-litre bioreactors, achieved good manufacturing practice (GMP) readiness six months ahead of schedule. Lotte also held a completion ceremony for the facility in November.

The new capacity will allow Lotte to manufacture biologic drug substances and finished products, positioning it to serve pharmaceutical companies seeking integrated manufacturing services across different stages of production.

Lotte expands into biopharmaceutical manufacturing

Lotte Biologics was established in 2022 as part of the wider Lotte Group’s expansion into life sciences.

The conglomerate, founded in the late 1960s, has established operations across food and beverages, retail, chemicals, hospitality and services.

The group’s move into biopharmaceuticals followed its consideration of an investment in South Korean biotechnology company Enzychem Lifesciences in 2021.

After the proposed transaction fell through, Lotte established Lotte Biologics and subsequently acquired the Syracuse manufacturing facility.

The combination of its US operations and new South Korean manufacturing capacity is intended to support pharmaceutical customers across multiple markets, as demand for outsourced biologics production continues to create opportunities for CDMOs.
